screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intracervical nitroprusside gel immediately prior to IUD placement; primary outcome was subject-reported pain with insertion.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ibuprofen 800 mg 30–45 minutes before insertion; pain measured by VAS at insertion.
Randomized trial on full bladder vs immediate emptying targeted ease of insertion; not an analgesic/anesthetic intervention to prevent insertion pain (pain reported but not primary/preventive focus).
Randomized, open-label trial comparing 2% intracervical lidocaine injection vs oral NSAID (ibuprofen) before LNG-IUS insertion; patient-reported pain assessed immediately, 2h, and 6h post-insertion.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 800 mg ibuprofen 45 minutes prior to LNG-IUS insertion; pain at tenaculum placement and insertion measured by VAS.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 400 μg vaginal misoprostol vs placebo 3h pre-insertion; included VAS pain during insertion.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (nulliparous) of 400 mcg buccal misoprostol vs placebo 90 minutes pre-insertion; VAS pain at multiple timepoints including insertion.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 400 mcg sublingual misoprostol vs placebo 3h pre-repeat LNG-IUS insertion; pain at insertion recorded.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 400 mg ibuprofen 45+ minutes pre-insertion; immediate post-insertion VAS pain recorded.
Single-blind randomized trial of 400 μg sublingual misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1h pre-insertion (C-section–only parous women); insertion-related pain reported.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ibuprofen 600 mg peri-insertion (before, 4–6h, and next morning); pain at insertion and within first 6h measured.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing oral tramadol 50 mg, naproxen 550 mg, and placebo 1h before insertion; insertion VAS pain as primary outcome.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (nulliparous) of 400 mcg buccal misoprostol vs placebo; provider ease and patient pain (VAS) including post-insertion measured.
Randomized, double-blind trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo prior to sounding/insertion; pain VAS at multiple peri-insertion points.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of 0.5 mg vaginal nitroglycerin gel 30 minutes pre-LNG-IUS insertion; patient-reported procedural pain measured.
Randomized trial of 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no local anesthetic prior to IUD insertion; VAS pain at insertion and immediate postprocedure measured.
Randomized, double-blind controlled trial comparing 2% lidocaine gel, lubricant gel, and no intervention placed intracervically; insertion pain VAS measured.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot of intrauterine 2% lidocaine infusion vs saline 3 minutes pre-insertion; tenaculum and insertion pain measured.
Randomized controlled trial in nulliparous women: sublingual 400 μg misoprostol + diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1h pre-insertion; insertion pain VAS (1–10) recorded.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial in nulligravidas: 400 μg vaginal misoprostol 4h pre-insertion vs placebo; reported reduced moderate-to-severe pain at insertion.
Randomized aromatherapy trial: inhaled lavender vs placebo 30 minutes pre-insertion; anxiety primary, but insertion pain measured (VAS).
Randomized, double-blind trial in nulliparous women: self-administered 400 μg misoprostol vs placebo 3–4h pre-insertion (vaginal or buccal); pain before, at, and after insertion measured.
Randomized, placebo-controlled phase II trial of a novel topical (portio/cervix/uterus) lidocaine formulation; insertion pain reduced vs placebo.

Prospective, single-blinded, controlled (placebo and no-treatment arms) paracervical 1% lidocaine block vs controls; insertion and tenaculum pain VAS measured. Randomization not explicit; include with caution. Randomization not explicit at abstract stage; including conservatively.
Randomized trial (registered) of 400 μg misoprostol vs placebo prior to insertion; primary outcome: pain at time of insertion (VAS).
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of self-administered 2% vaginal lidocaine gel 5 minutes pre-insertion; pain at multiple peri-insertion points recorded.
